itineraryStops[0].description: **Pickup is consolidated at four central Jeju City points** to minimize morning crisscrossing: **Jeju International Airport (제주공항)** for guests with same-day arrivals or hotels near the airport corridor; **Jeju City Hall (제주시청)** for guests in the Yeon-dong / Nohyeong / Old Town hotel cluster; **Hagwi-dong (하귀동)** as the westernmost pickup before heading east; and **Dongmun Traditional Market (동문시장)** as the optional eastern Jeju City pickup near Tapdong waterfront. Sequence is Hagwi → Airport → City Hall → Dongmun → eastward Route 1132 toward Hamdeok. The minicoach is **small-group (max ~14 pax)** with English-speaking guide. **Bilingual printed itinerary card** distributed at pickup, weather brief at first stop.

itineraryStops[1].name: Hamdeok Seoubong Beach
itineraryStops[1].category: Top-3 Jeju Beach — Olle Trail 19 + WWII Coastal History
itineraryStops[1].description: **Hamdeok Seoubong Beach (함덕 서우봉 해변)** is consistently ranked among **Jeju's top 3 beaches**, defined by the contrast between **white-sand beach (~500 m main stretch, 3 connected coves totaling ~900 m)** and the **adjacent volcanic cone Seoubong (서우봉, 'Cow Looking Like a Cow's Head' parasitic cone)** rising directly from the eastern end. The water's signature **emerald-turquoise color** comes from shallow coral-sand seabed reflecting through clear ocean — the Mediterranean-like contrast (rare in Korea) is what made Hamdeok one of the country's most photographed domestic beach destinations. The beach can absorb up to **50,000 daily visitors** at peak summer, but spring + autumn visits are typically uncrowded. **Seoubong Peak** (climbable ~1 hour to summit) wears **canola-yellow slopes in spring (March–April)** and offers a **panoramic eastward view to Manjanggul lava-tube area**. **Historical layer**: the sea cliffs immediately west of Seoubong hold **Imperial Japanese Army tunnels carved during WWII colonial occupation** — kamikaze suicide-boat shelters and ammunition stores, similar to the 18 caves at Seongsan Ilchulbong. The tunnels are publicly accessible (with signage explaining the historical context). The beach is the **central segment of Jeju Olle Trail Course 19 (조천 → 김녕)**, marked with the trail's signature blue-orange ribbons. **Cafe Delmoondo (델문도 카페)** anchors the beachfront — large terraces, sea-view, popular for Instagram and casual stops. **FREE admission**; the beach is **20 km / ~40-min drive from Jeju International Airport** on Route 1132.

itineraryStops[1].whyOnRoute: **Coastal opening anchor of the eastern UNESCO route**. Hamdeok establishes the day's first dual frame: **natural beauty (top-3 beach) + WWII colonial history (tunnels)** — a deliberate setup for the day's recurring pattern of **paired natural + historical layers** (continuing at Seongsan with its 18 caves, and at the Haenyeo Museum where diving heritage meets UNESCO Intangible designation). Geographically, Hamdeok is the **natural first stop after Jeju City**, just 40 min east on Route 1132, before the long inland transit to Seongeup. Compared with **Woljeongri Beach (further east, no WWII history)** or **Iho Tewoo Beach (Jeju City, no Olle trail anchor)**, Hamdeok is **on-route, FREE, and historically layered** — the highest-yield east-coast beach stop. Morning timing also catches the **9:50–10:50 low-flat lighting** before midday harshness.

itineraryStops[2].name: Seongeup Folk Village (UNESCO heritage)
itineraryStops[2].category: Joseon-era Walled Town — Important Folklore Cultural Heritage (1423 founding)
itineraryStops[2].description: **Seongeup Folk Village (성읍 민속마을)** is a **living Joseon-era walled town founded in 1423** during the reign of **Sejong the Great** as Jeong-eui-hyeon (정의현), one of the three administrative seats of Joseon-era Jeju. The village served continuously as a **county administrative center until 1914** — nearly **500 years** — and retains **110 traditional structures** today within the original eupseong (읍성) walled-town footprint, designed on **Korean feng shui principles** typical of Joseon county capitals. The entire village is designated **Important Folklore Cultural Heritage of South Korea**, with **multiple individual buildings** carrying separate heritage status. At the village center stand **two ancient trees designated Natural Monuments of South Korea** — a **Saw-leaf Zelkova (느티나무)** and a **Japanese Hackberry (팽나무)**, both estimated **600+ years old** and revered as the village's spiritual anchor. Historical scars are visible: a **major fire in 1826 destroyed ~80 buildings**, and the village suffered fire damage **during the Jeju Uprising in 1948** — both events preserved as historical record on village signage. The **peak household count (historical, pre-modern) was ~1,500** — today the village remains inhabited by ~250 families, many actively maintaining traditional crafts. Drama filming credit: **'Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace)' (MBC, 2003–2004)**, the international K-drama hit. Local specialty: **Omegisul (오메기술)** — a **rice-based traditional Jeju liquor** brewed by **one family for multiple generations**, with the brewing demonstrated and tasted free of charge at the home-brewery within the village. **FREE admission**; outdoor walking dominates (~70% outdoor / 30% indoor for individual hanok visits).

itineraryStops[3].name: Micheon Cave at Ilchul Land (Manjanggul alternate)
itineraryStops[3].category: Lava Tube + Theme Park — Manjanggul Alternate (UNESCO-property adjacent)
itineraryStops[3].description: **Ilchul Land (일출랜드)** is a **400,000 m² nature theme park** in Seongsan, opened **2002**, built around the **Micheon Cave (미천굴)** lava tube — a **1,700 m total length cave** with a **365 m artificially leveled walk-through section** open to visitors (~25-minute traverse). The cave is part of Jeju's **lava-tube system that shares geological lineage with Manjanggul Cave** — the UNESCO World Natural Heritage lava tube — and **functions as the operational alternate when Manjanggul closes for conservation maintenance or weather (typhoons, freezing)**. Where Manjanggul preserves its uneven natural floor as an authentic geological experience, Micheon's leveled walkway makes the cave **accessible to elderly visitors, families with strollers, and guests with mobility limitations** — a deliberate engineering choice that broadens the lava-tube experience to audiences who couldn't navigate Manjanggul. The interior is lit with **decorative seven-color lighting (gold, silver, bronze, red, black, blue, white)** highlighting cave formations — controversial among purists but practical for non-specialist tourist photography. Outside the cave, the park extends across **Subyeon Park, a reconstructed traditional Jeju village, Wild Flower Bonsai Garden, Cactus Greenhouse, Sculpture Street, and a Footbath Cafe (aroma foot spa)** — making this the **only Jeju attraction with an on-site Muslim prayer room** (a deliberate accessibility investment). Drama filming credit: **'Running Man' (런닝맨, SBS) Episode 89 (Alice-in-Wonderland themed, 2012)**. Admission: **Adult ₩12,000 / Youth ₩9,000 / Child ₩7,000**. Indoor/outdoor split is **30% indoor (cave + greenhouse)** / **70% outdoor (park grounds)** — meaningful for weather-flexibility planning.

itineraryStops[4].name: Lunch (Jeju local restaurant)
itineraryStops[4].category: Midday Reset — East Jeju Local Cuisine
itineraryStops[4].description: **60-minute reset between Ilchulland and Seongsan Ilchulbong** — Seongsan-eup harbor-side restaurant strip catches daily seafood landings. Default rotation: **mulhoe (물회, cold raw-fish soup)** in summer (June–September), **galchi-jorim (갈치조림, braised cutlassfish)** in winter (October–February), or **heuk-doeji gui (흑돼지구이, Jeju black pig BBQ)** year-round. Black pig is a heritage breed designated **Cultural Heritage Material No. 5 (2015)**. **Vegetarian + halal-friendly options** available at one venue in the rotation — disclose at pickup. Lunch venue is **10-min coach to Seongsan Ilchulbong** entrance — minimal post-lunch transit before the afternoon climb.

itineraryStops[5].name: Seongsan Ilchulbong (UNESCO Sunrise Peak)
itineraryStops[5].category: UNESCO Tuff Cone — Sunrise Peak (Triple UNESCO Designation)
itineraryStops[5].description: **Seongsan Ilchulbong (성산일출봉, 'Sunrise Peak')** is a **5,000-year-old Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic tuff cone** — a rare landform created when an underwater basalt eruption broke the sea surface, the magma met seawater, and the resulting steam-explosive ash built a **182 m fortress-shaped crater** rim instead of a typical lava cone. The result is what UNESCO formally calls **'an exceptional example of an emergent Surtseyan-type volcanic edifice'**. The crater is **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** that local lore likens to a stone crown. Seongsan carries the **Triple UNESCO designation**: **World Natural Heritage (inscribed 2007-07-02)** as part of the **'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' property**, **Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Global Geopark (2010-10)** — a stack matched only by Hallasan itself among Korean sites. **18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** (kamikaze suicide-boat shelters, 1945) are tunneled into the seaward base. Trail: **0.8 km one-way, ~140 m elevation gain, 60 min round trip** on wide stone steps. **Haenyeo (해녀) demonstrations** run **daily at 13:30 and 15:00** at the rocky cove below the cone — Jeju women divers (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2016) descend without scuba gear. Admission updated **April 2025**: **Adult ₩5,000 / Youth+Child ₩2,500 / Group adult ₩1,600**, free under 7 and over 65. The summit deck is also part of the **Yeongjusipgyeong (Jeju 10 Scenic Wonders) canon**, and remains Korea's premier **annual New Year sunrise pilgrimage** destination — 50,000+ visitors ascend before dawn on January 1, with municipal sunrise-festival programming since 1995. **Udo Island (우도, 'Cow Island')** — Korea's largest secondary volcanic island — is clearly visible 4 km offshore from the summit, accessible by **15-min ferry from Seongsan Port** (₩10,500 round-trip) for guests with extra time on a different itinerary.

itineraryStops[6].name: Haenyeo Museum (women divers)
itineraryStops[6].category: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Anchor — Jeju Diving Culture (2016)
itineraryStops[6].description: **Jeju Haenyeo Museum (제주 해녀 박물관)** is the institutional anchor for **'Culture of Jeju Haenyeo (women divers)'** — inscribed as **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016**. Located in **Gujwa-eup**, the museum sits in the heart of Jeju's most haenyeo-active eastern coastal villages. The earliest written record of Jeju women divers dates to **1629**, in **'Description of Jeju's Natural Features' and 'Collected Works of Guchang' by Lee Geon (이건)**, where they were called **'Jamnyeo (潛女, diving women)'** — though oral tradition holds that the diving practice is far older, possibly **predating Joseon by centuries**. The museum documents the haenyeo's distinctive practice across **3 exhibition halls**: **(1) Daily Life + Equipment** — traditional diving gear (pre-rubber-suit cotton suits, *tewak* gourd floats, *bitchang* hand-spear, weighted nets), kitchen tools, and the **maternal lineage of dive-teaching** (mothers train daughters from age 6–7); **(2) Diving Practice + Categorization** — haenyeo are formally graded as **Hagun (junior, trainee), Junggun (mid-level), Sanggun (senior, who guides the others)**, with depth and breath-hold capacity defining rank; senior haenyeo dive to **10 m on a single 60-second breath-hold**, working **~7 hours per day, ~90 days per year**; **(3) Community + Future** — village cooperatives, ritual songs, the **diminishing population (under 4,000 active today, mostly 70+)**, and conservation efforts. Outdoor sculpture garden + replica fishing boat at the entrance courtyard. Admission: **Adult ₩1,100 / Youth ₩500 / FREE under 7 + over 65**. Hours: **09:00–18:00**, **closed Tuesdays and lunar new year/Chuseok**. Indoor ratio ~80% — strong rainy-day fallback anchor.

itineraryStops[6].whyOnRoute: **UNESCO Intangible heritage finale** — and the day's narrative climax. After the morning's natural + colonial-history layers (Hamdeok), the Joseon administrative heritage (Seongeup), the lava-tube UNESCO adjacency (Ilchulland), and the Triple UNESCO geological climax (Seongsan), the Haenyeo Museum **completes the day's UNESCO narrative arc** with UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status (2016). Geographically this is **15-min coach from Seongsan**, the natural sequencing — guests who watched the 15:00 haenyeo demonstration at Seongsan now learn the full historical and cultural depth in museum context. **Indoor ratio ~80%** = the day's strongest rainy-day fallback anchor, also a welcome interior break after the Seongsan climb. Compared with **Jeju Folk Village Museum (themed reconstruction, ₩12,000)** or **Jeju National Museum (Jeju City center, off-route)**, the Haenyeo Museum is **₩1,100, on-route, and UNESCO-grade** — the highest yield for the day's UNESCO theme.

routeShapeIntro.title: How this day flows
routeShapeIntro.subtitle: An eastern-Jeju loop covering the island's two UNESCO highlights from the east — Seongsan Ilchulbong (Natural Heritage) and the Haenyeo women-diver tradition (Intangible Cultural Heritage) — plus the heritage anchor of Seongeup Folk Village and the Micheon Cave lava tube as the current Manjanggul alternate. The 4.9/5 rating across 1,148 reviews is the highest of the operator's tour family, and the all-admissions-included structure (Seongsan ₩5,000, Seongeup, Micheon Cave, Haenyeo Museum) saves visitors approximately ₩20,000 vs. paying à la carte.

whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[0].title: Why this route is built this way
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[0].items: Both UNESCO listings (natural + cultural) in one day

Most Jeju eastern tours include Seongsan Ilchulbong but skip the Haenyeo Museum. This route deliberately keeps both — meaning visitors leave with both Jeju UNESCO categories: the natural heritage (Seongsan's tuff cone) and the intangible cultural heritage (haenyeo women-diver tradition, listed 2016).

Manjanggul Lava Tube is currently closed — most tours either skip cave content entirely or substitute lazily. This route uses Micheon Cave at Ilchul Land, which gives visitors a comparable lava-tube experience plus the Ilchul Land botanical garden (seasonal flower displays). When Manjanggul reopens, the operator will likely revert; check at booking.
All admissions included — value at the price tier

Eastern Jeju has more paid attractions than southern Jeju (Seongsan ₩5,000, Ilchul Land ₩12,000, Haenyeo Museum ₩1,100). Including all of them in the base price saves ≈ ₩18,000 per person versus the standard à-la-carte structure of competing tours.

The 30-minute rim climb is steep and not for everyone. The route allocates 90 minutes total at the site, which is enough for the climb if you want it but also enough to walk the free coastal trail at the base for similar photo angles without the stairs. Visitors with mobility concerns get the UNESCO credit either way.

staticQuestions[0].question: Will I see live haenyeo divers?
staticQuestions[0].answer: The Haenyeo Museum has video footage of working dives. Live diving demonstrations sometimes happen at the adjacent harbor or at Seongsan Ilchulbong's base (typically 13:30 and 15:00 daily, weather-permitting). The tour timing increases the chance but does not guarantee a live demonstration.
staticQuestions[1].question: Can I skip the Seongsan rim climb?
staticQuestions[1].answer: Yes — the free coastal trail at the base offers similar photo angles without the stairs. The 90-minute stop window accommodates either choice. Visitors with mobility concerns or who prefer a calmer pace use the coastal trail.
staticQuestions[2].question: How is this different from the Southern UNESCO tour?
staticQuestions[2].answer: Same operator. The Southern tour covers Hallasan trail, Camellia Hill, Cheonjeyeon Falls, Jusangjeolli, O'sulloc — focused on natural heritage and gardens. This Eastern tour covers Hamdeok Beach, Seongeup Village, Micheon Cave, Seongsan, and the Haenyeo Museum — focused on UNESCO heritage (both natural and cultural) and traditional Jeju life. Most 2-day Jeju visitors do one of each.
staticQuestions[3].question: What if Manjanggul reopens during my visit?
staticQuestions[3].answer: If Manjanggul (a more famous and longer lava tube than Micheon) reopens, the operator may swap the cave stop. Manjanggul is currently closed for ongoing safety repairs with no announced reopening date — the Micheon Cave alternate is the dependable substitute.
staticQuestions[4].question: Is lunch included?
staticQuestions[4].answer: No — lunch is at your own expense (≈ ₩15,000). The guide will recommend a local east-Jeju restaurant and assist with vegetarian, vegan, halal, or allergy needs if you advise at booking.
staticQuestions[5].question: Why airport Gate 1 instead of Gate 3?
staticQuestions[5].answer: The Eastern tour pickup uses Jeju Airport Gate 1 (1st Floor Domestic Arrivals) because the airport-to-east-coast route is more efficient via the eastern airport perimeter road. The Southern tour uses Gate 3 (3rd Floor Domestic Departures) for the southern route. This is operational; pick whichever tour is in your plan and follow the gate listed on your booking.
staticQuestions[6].question: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to eastern Jeju?
staticQuestions[6].answer: Yes — it covers the most distinctive stops in the area in a single balanced day.
staticQuestions[7].question: Is the walking difficult?
staticQuestions[7].answer: An active day with several walking-heavy stops.
staticQuestions[8].question: Is this tour suitable for families?
staticQuestions[8].answer: Yes for families whose kids can handle a full day of moving around.
staticQuestions[9].question: Can older adults join comfortably?
staticQuestions[9].answer: Recommended only for active seniors comfortable with stairs and uneven ground.
staticQuestions[10].question: What's the recommended minimum age?
staticQuestions[10].answer: Best fit is around age 10 and up — children comfortable with a full-day rhythm and the walking notes above.

page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[1]: ≈ 20 km east of Jeju International Airport, on Jeju Olle Trail Course 19. The beach forms three coves stretching ≈ 900 m, with white sand made of fine shell fragments and shallow emerald water. The east end is anchored by Seoubong oreum (서우봉 — 'rhinoceros-cow peak'), a small volcanic cone historically used as a beacon-fire signal station communicating with Wondangbong and Satgat oreum. On clear days the view from the upper coastal walk reaches Hallasan.

page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[2]: A 600-year continuously inhabited village, founded 1423 as the administrative seat of Jeongui-hyeon — one of three Joseon-era administrative divisions of Jeju (alongside Jeju-mok and Daejeong-hyeon). Designated National Folklore Cultural Heritage in 1984. Inside the Jeongui Hyeonseong fortress wall: thatched-roof homes still inhabited by residents, the Jeongui Hyanggyo Confucian school (Jeju Tangible Cultural Asset No. 5), the Ilgwanheon government office, centuries-old zelkova and nettle trees, dol hareubang stone statues, and traditional tongsi (combined pigsty/outhouse). Note: Seongeup is Korea's national folklore designation; it is NOT a UNESCO site (the heading on this stop is shorthand for 'cultural heritage,' not UNESCO inscription).

Privately-managed lava tube at Ilchul Land theme park near Pyoseon — distinct from the UNESCO-listed Manjanggul on Jeju's north coast. We use this stop because it's compatible with the Eastern route's pacing; Manjanggul is on a different coast and would add ≈ 90 min of driving.

page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[0: Will I see live haenyeo divers?

The Haenyeo Museum has video footage of working dives. Live diving demonstrations sometimes happen at the adjacent harbor or at Seongsan Ilchulbong's base (typically 13:30 and 15:00 daily, weather-permitting). The tour timing increases the chance but does not guarantee a live demonstration.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[1: Can I skip the Seongsan rim climb?

Yes — the free coastal trail at the base offers similar photo angles without the stairs. The 90-minute stop window accommodates either choice. Visitors with mobility concerns or who prefer a calmer pace use the coastal trail.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[2: How is this different from the Southern UNESCO tour?

Same operator. The Southern tour covers Hallasan trail, Camellia Hill, Cheonjeyeon Falls, Jusangjeolli, O'sulloc — focused on natural heritage and gardens. This Eastern tour covers Hamdeok Beach, Seongeup Village, Micheon Cave, Seongsan, and the Haenyeo Museum — focused on UNESCO heritage (both natural and cultural) and traditional Jeju life. Most 2-day Jeju visitors do one of each.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[3: What if Manjanggul reopens during my visit?

If Manjanggul (a more famous and longer lava tube than Micheon) reopens, the operator may swap the cave stop. Manjanggul is currently closed for ongoing safety repairs with no announced reopening date — the Micheon Cave alternate is the dependable substitute.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[4: No — lunch is at your own expense (≈ ₩15,000). The guide will recommend a local east-Jeju restaurant and assist with vegetarian, vegan, halal, or allergy needs if you advise at booking.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[5: Why airport Gate 1 instead of Gate 3?

The Eastern tour pickup uses Jeju Airport Gate 1 (1st Floor Domestic Arrivals) because the airport-to-east-coast route is more efficient via the eastern airport perimeter road. The Southern tour uses Gate 3 (3rd Floor Domestic Departures) for the southern route. This is operational; pick whichever tour is in your plan and follow the gate listed on your booking.

Yes — it covers the most distinctive stops in the area in a single balanced day.
